key_insight: FOCUS uses selective branching during reinforcement learning to help a critic learn better value estimates for intermediate steps. The goal is to improve learning from delayed rewards without repeatedly sampling continuations at every point.
problem_solved: Long-horizon language-model agents struggle to identify which earlier actions contributed to a final outcome. Learned critics can give inaccurate guidance, while estimating intermediate values through repeated continuation sampling is costly.
method: Train a critic to estimate the value of intermediate states in an agent’s trajectory.
Selectively branch from points within trajectories to gather additional evidence for critic learning.
Use selective sampling to address the trade-off between value-estimation quality and continuation-sampling cost.
impact: FOCUS offers a potentially more efficient way to train agents on tasks with many steps and sparse feedback. The provided abstract is incomplete, so quantitative gains and experimental results cannot be assessed.
visual_elements: A long action timeline with a reward only at the endpoint, illustrating delayed credit assignment.
A trajectory tree with only selected intermediate states branching into additional continuations.
A critic icon beside intermediate states, displaying estimated future value.
A conceptual comparison of sampling everywhere versus selective branching, highlighting computational cost.
paper_title: FOCUS: Active Critic Learning for Long-Horizon Language Model Agents
paper_authors: Zhengping Jiang, William Jurayj, Liaoyaqi Wang, Chunsheng Zuo, Anqi Liu
